sanskrit: śaravarṣair mahāvegair amitrān abhivarṣataḥ mad anyaṃ nānupaśyāmi prativīraṃ tavāhave
english: As you rain upon your foes torrents of arrows of tremendous force, I see no champion in this battle fit to stand against you save myself.

sanskrit: rathadviradapattyaśvān ekaḥ pramathase bahūn mṛgasaṃghān ivāraṇye vibhīr bhīmabalo hariḥ
english: Single-handed you crush chariots, elephants, foot-soldiers, and horsemen in their multitudes, as a fearless lion of terrible strength crushes herds of deer in the forest.

sanskrit: mahatā rathaghoṣeṇa divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca nādayan varṣānte sasyahā pītho bhābhir āpūrayann iva
english: With the mighty roar of your chariot you make heaven and earth resound, as the sun at the rains' end, drinking up the grain-fields, floods all things with his rays.

sanskrit: saṃspṛśānaḥ śarāṃs tīkṣṇāṃs tūṇād āśīviṣopamān mayaivaikena yudhyasva tryambakeṇāndhako yathā
english: Drawing keen shafts from your quiver, like venomous serpents, do battle with me alone, as the Andhaka demon fought with the three-eyed Rudra.

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety uktvā prahareti ca tāḍitaḥ karṇinā droṇatanayaṃ vivyādha malayadhvajaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the king of the Malaya banner answered, "So be it," and crying "Strike!" he pierced the son of Droṇa with a barbed arrow.

sanskrit: marmabhedibhir atyugrair bāṇair agniśikhopamaiḥ smayann abhyahanad drauṇiḥ pāṇḍyam ācāryasattamaḥ
english: Then Droṇa's son, foremost of the teacher's line, smiling, struck the Pāṇḍya king with vital-piercing, terrible arrows that resembled tongues of flame.

sanskrit: tato navāparāṃs tīkṣṇān nārācān kaṅkavāsasaḥ gatyā daśamyā saṃyuktān aśvatthāmā vyavāsṛjat
english: Then Aśvatthāman loosed nine more sharp iron shafts, fledged with heron feathers and endowed with the tenfold speed of flight.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ pañcācchinat pāṇḍyaḥ pañcabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ catvāro 'bhyāhanan vāhān āśu te vyasavo 'bhavan
english: Of these the Pāṇḍya cut five apart with five whetted arrows; the remaining four struck his horses, and they were swiftly bereft of life.

sanskrit: atha droṇasutasyeṣūṃs tāṃś chittvā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ dhanurjyāṃ vitatāṃ pāṇḍyaś cicchedādityavarcasaḥ
english: Then, having cut those arrows of Droṇa's son with whetted shafts, the Pāṇḍya, splendid as the sun, severed the drawn bowstring.

sanskrit: vijyaṃ dhanur athādhijyaṃ kṛtvā drauṇir amitrahā tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi preṣayām āsa pāṇḍyataḥ iṣusaṃbādham ākāśam akarod diśa eva ca
english: Restringing his unstrung bow, Droṇa's son, the slayer of foes, sent forth thousands of arrows at the Pāṇḍya, choking the sky and all the quarters with shafts.

sanskrit: tatas tān asyataḥ sarvān drauṇer bāṇān mahātmanaḥ jānāno 'py akṣayān pāṇḍyo 'śātayat puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍya, that bull among men, though he knew the arrows of the great-souled Droṇi to be inexhaustible, cut down all those that were hurled at him.

sanskrit: prahitāṃs tān prayatnena chittvā drauṇer iṣūn ariḥ cakrarakṣau tatas tasya prāṇudan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having with effort cut those arrows that Droṇi sped at him, the foe then drove off his two wheel-guards with whetted shafts.

sanskrit: athārer lāghavaṃ dṛṣṭvā maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukaḥ prāsyad droṇasuto bāṇān vṛṣṭiṃ pūṣānujo yathā
english: Then, seeing the deftness of his foe, Droṇa's son bent his bow into a circle and let fly his arrows in a downpour, as the younger brother of Pūṣan pours down rain.

sanskrit: aṣṭāv aṣṭagavāny ūhuḥ śakaṭāni yad āyudham ahnas tad aṣṭabhāgena drauṇiś cikṣepa māriṣa
english: That store of weapons which eight wagons, each drawn by eight oxen, bore away — all that, O honoured one, Droṇi hurled in an eighth part of a day.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddham antakālāntakopamam ye ye dadṛśire tatra visaṃjñāḥ prāyaśo 'bhavan
english: Whoever looked upon him there — wrathful as Death itself, like the destroyer at the end of time — most of them fell senseless.

sanskrit: parjanya iva gharmānte vṛṣṭyā sādridrumāṃ mahīm ācāryaputras tāṃ senāṃ bāṇavṛṣṭyābhyavīvṛṣat
english: As the rain-cloud at summer's end drenches with its showers the earth with its mountains and trees, so the teacher's son drenched that army with a downpour of arrows.

sanskrit: drauṇiparjanyamuktāṃ tāṃ bāṇavṛṣṭiṃ suduḥsahām vāyavyāstreṇa sa kṣipraṃ ruddhvā pāṇḍyānilo 'nadat
english: That well-nigh unbearable rain of arrows loosed by the cloud that was Droṇi, the Pāṇḍya, a very wind, swiftly checked with the weapon of Vāyu, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: tasya nānadataḥ ketuṃ candanāgurubhūṣitam malayapratimaṃ drauṇiś chittvāśvāṃś caturo 'hanat
english: As he roared, Droṇi cut down his standard, adorned with sandal and aloe and rising like the Malaya mountain, and slew his four horses.

sanskrit: sūtam ekeṣuṇā hatvā mahājaladanisvanam dhanuś chittvārdhacandreṇa vyadhamat tilaśo ratham
english: Slaying his charioteer with a single arrow, with a crescent-headed shaft he cut his bow, loud as a great thundercloud, and shattered his chariot to fragments fine as sesame.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya chittvā sarvāyudhāni ca prāptam apy ahitaṃ drauṇir na jaghāna raṇepsayā
english: Having warded off weapon with weapon and cut all the foe's arms apart, Droṇi, though his enemy was now in his power, did not slay him, in his longing for the fight.

sanskrit: hateśvaro dantivaraḥ sukalpitas; tvarābhisṛṣṭaḥ pratiśarmago balī tam adhyatiṣṭhan malayeśvaro mahān; yathādriśṛṅgaṃ harir unnadaṃs tathā
english: A noble, well-caparisoned elephant, its driver slain, was sent in haste against him; armoured and mighty, the great lord of Malaya mounted it, as a lion roaring climbs a mountain peak.

sanskrit: sa tomaraṃ bhāskararaśmisaṃnibhaṃ; balāstrasargottamayatnamanyubhiḥ sasarja śīghraṃ pratipīḍayan gajaṃ; guroḥ sutāyādripatīśvaro nadan
english: Goading the elephant, the lord of the mountain-king, roaring, swiftly hurled at the teacher's son a lance bright as the sun's rays, with all the force, fury, and supreme effort of his weapon's release.

sanskrit: maṇipratānottamavajrahāṭakair; alaṃkṛtaṃ cāṃśukamālyamauktikaiḥ hato 'sy asāv ity asakṛn mudā nadan; parābhinad drauṇivarāṅgabhūṣaṇam
english: That lance, adorned with strings of gems, fine diamonds and gold, with silk, garlands and pearls, he drove home, crying again and again in his joy, "You are slain!" — and it pierced the splendid ornament on Droṇi's body.

sanskrit: tad arkacandragrahapāvakatviṣaṃ; bhṛśābhighātāt patitaṃ vicūrṇitam mahendravajrābhihataṃ mahāvanaṃ; yathādriśṛṅgaṃ dharaṇītale tathā
english: That ornament, gleaming like the sun, moon, planets and fire, fell shattered to powder by the violent blow, as a great forest on a mountain peak, smitten by mighty Indra's bolt, falls to the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajajvāla pareṇa manyunā; padāhato nāgapatir yathā tathā samādadhe cāntakadaṇḍasaṃnibhān; iṣūn amitrāntakarāṃś caturdaśa
english: Then he blazed up with surpassing fury, like a serpent-king trodden underfoot, and fitted to his bow fourteen arrows like the rod of Death, makers of an end to foes.

sanskrit: dvipasya pādāgrakarān sa pañcabhir; nṛpasya bāhū ca śiro 'tha ca tribhiḥ jaghāna ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣaḍ ṛtūttamatviṣaḥ; sa pāṇḍyarājānucarān mahārathān
english: With five he struck off the elephant's feet and trunk, with three the king's arms and head, and with six he slew the six great car-warriors who followed the Pāṇḍya king, splendid as the six seasons.

sanskrit: sudīrghavṛttau varacandanokṣitau; suvarṇamuktāmaṇivajrabhūṣitau bhujau dharāyāṃ patitau nṛpasya tau; viveṣṭatus tārkṣyahatāv ivoragau
english: The king's two arms, long and rounded, anointed with choice sandal, decked with gold, pearls, gems and diamonds, fell to the earth and writhed there like serpents struck down by Garuḍa.

sanskrit: śiraś ca tat pūrṇaśaśiprabhānanaṃ; saroṣatāmrāyatanetram unnasam kṣitau vibabhrāja patat sakuṇḍalaṃ; viśākhayor madhyagataḥ śaśī yathā
english: And his head, its face bright as the full moon, with long eyes coppery in wrath and a high-bridged nose, falling earthward with its earrings, shone like the moon set between the two Viśākhā stars.

sanskrit: samāptavidyaṃ tu guroḥ sutaṃ nṛpaḥ; samāptakarmāṇam upetya te sutaḥ suhṛdvṛto 'tyartham apūjayan mudā; jite balau viṣṇum ivāmareśvaraḥ
english: Then your son the king, approaching the teacher's son — perfect in his learning, his deed accomplished — surrounded by his friends, honoured him exceedingly with joy, as the lord of the immortals honoured Viṣṇu when Bali was conquered.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca pāṇḍye hate kim akarod arjuno yudhi saṃjaya ekavīreṇa karṇena drāviteṣu pareṣu ca
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the Pāṇḍya was slain, Saṃjaya, what did Arjuna do in the battle, and when the foe had been driven off by Karṇa, that lone champion?

sanskrit: samāptavidyo balavān yukto vīraś ca pāṇḍavaḥ sarvabhūteṣv anujñātaḥ śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā
english: Perfect in learning, mighty, disciplined, a hero is that son of Pāṇḍu, granted favour over all beings by the great-souled Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: tasmān mahad bhayaṃ tīvram amitraghnād dhanaṃjayāt sa yat tatrākarot pārthas tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Grievous and keen is the fear that comes from Dhanaṃjaya, slayer of foes. Tell me, Saṃjaya, what Pārtha did there.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hate pāṇḍye 'rjunaṃ kṛṣṇas tvarann āha vaco hitam paśyātimānyaṃ rājānam apayātāṃś ca pāṇḍavān
english: Saṃjaya said: When the Pāṇḍya was slain, Kṛṣṇa hastily spoke salutary words to Arjuna: "Behold the overproud king, and the Pāṇḍavas in retreat.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmnaś ca saṃkalpād dhatāḥ karṇena sṛñjayāḥ tathāśvanaranāgānāṃ kṛtaṃ ca kadanaṃ mahat ity ācaṣṭa sudurdharṣo vāsudevaḥ kirīṭine
english: By Aśvatthāman's resolve and by Karṇa the Sṛñjayas have been slain, and great is the slaughter wrought among horses, men, and elephants" — thus the unassailable Vāsudeva spoke to the diademed one.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā ca dṛṣṭvā ca bhrātur ghoraṃ mahad bhayam vāhayāśvān hṛṣīkeśa kṣipram ity āha pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Having heard this and seen the terrible, great peril to his brothers, the son of Pāṇḍu said, "Hṛṣīkeśa, drive the horses on, swiftly!"

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyād dhṛṣīkeśo rathenāpratiyodhinā dāruṇaś ca punas tatra prādurāsīt samāgamaḥ
english: Then Hṛṣīkeśa set forth with that chariot none could withstand, and once more a fearful encounter arose there.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte bhūyaḥ saṃgrāmo rājasattama karṇasya pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yamarāṣṭravivardhanaḥ
english: Then again, O best of kings, a battle broke out between Karṇa and the Pāṇḍavas, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi bāṇān parighān asitomarapaṭṭiśān musalāni bhuśuṇḍīś ca śaktiṛṣṭiparaśvadhān
english: Bows, arrows, iron clubs, swords, lances, spears, maces, slings, javelins, daggers, and battle-axes —

sanskrit: gadāḥ prāsān asīn kuntān bhiṇḍipālān mahāṅkuśān pragṛhya kṣipram āpetuḥ parasparajigīṣayā
english: maces, darts, swords, spears, slings, and great goads — seizing these, the warriors swiftly fell upon one another, each longing to overcome the rest.

sanskrit: bāṇajyātalaśabdena dyāṃ diśaḥ pradiśo viyat pṛthivīṃ nemighoṣeṇa nādayanto 'bhyayuḥ parān
english: Making heaven, the quarters, the intermediate points, and the sky resound with the noise of arrows, bowstrings and palm-guards, and the earth with the rumble of chariot-wheels, they rushed upon their foes.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā saṃhṛṣṭāś cakrur āhavam vīrā vīrair mahāghoraṃ kalahāntaṃ titīrṣavaḥ
english: Thrilled by that mighty din, the heroes joined battle with heroes, fiercely terrible, each eager to fight the quarrel through to its end.

sanskrit: jyātalatradhanuḥśabdāḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca bṛṃhitam tāḍitānāṃ ca patatāṃ ninādaḥ sumahān abhūt
english: The sound of bowstrings, palm-guards and bows, the trumpeting of elephants, and the cries of the stricken as they fell — a tremendous uproar arose.

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdāṃś ca vividhāñ śūrāṇām abhigarjatām śrutvā śabdaṃ bhṛśaṃ tresur jaghnur mamluś ca bhārata
english: Hearing the manifold whistling of arrows and the roaring of the brave, O Bhārata, men trembled exceedingly, struck others down, and themselves grew faint.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ nānadyatāṃ caiva śastravṛṣṭiṃ ca muñcatām bahūn ādhirathiḥ karṇaḥ pramamātha raṇeṣubhiḥ
english: As they roared and loosed a rain of weapons, Karṇa, the son of Adhiratha, crushed many of them with his battle-shafts.

sanskrit: pañca pāñcālavīrāṇāṃ rathān daśa ca pañca ca sāśvasūtadhvajān karṇaḥ śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Fifteen chariots of the Pāñcāla heroes, with their horses, drivers, and standards, Karṇa with his arrows sent to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: yodhamukhyā mahāvīryāḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ karṇam āhave śīghrāstrā divam āvṛtya parivavruḥ samantataḥ
english: The foremost warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, of great valour and swift weapons, veiling the sky, surrounded Karṇa in the battle on every side.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo dviṣatsenāṃ śaravarṣair viloḍayan vijagāhe 'ṇḍajāpūrṇāṃ padminīm iva yūthapaḥ
english: Then Karṇa, churning the enemy host with showers of arrows, plunged into it as a lord of the herd plunges into a lotus-pond filled with birds.

sanskrit: dviṣanmadhyam avaskandya rādheyo dhanur uttamam vidhunvānaḥ śitair bāṇaiḥ śirāṃsy unmathya pātayat
english: Springing into the midst of the foe, the son of Rādhā, shaking his peerless bow, with sharpened arrows struck off heads and made them fall.

sanskrit: carmavarmāṇi saṃchindya nirvāpam iva dehinām viṣehur nāsya saṃparkaṃ dvitīyasya patatriṇaḥ
english: Cutting through shields and armour, as if extinguishing the lives of embodied beings, they could not endure the touch of a second of his winged shafts.

sanskrit: varmadehāsumathanair dhanuṣaḥ pracyutaiḥ śaraiḥ maurvyā talatrair nyavadhīt kaśayā vājino yathā
english: With arrows sped from his bow that shattered armour, body, and life, and with the bowstring and palm-guards, he slew them as a charioteer drives his horses with the whip.

sanskrit: pāṇḍusṛñjayapāñcālāñ śaragocaram ānayat mamarda karṇas tarasā siṃho mṛgagaṇān iva
english: He brought the Pāṇḍus, Sṛñjayas, and Pāñcālas within range of his arrows, and Karṇa crushed them with vehemence, as a lion crushes herds of deer.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāñcālaputrāś ca draupadeyāś ca māriṣa yamau ca yuyudhānaś ca sahitāḥ karṇam abhyayuḥ
english: Then, O honoured one, the sons of the Pāñcālas and the sons of Draupadī, the twins, and Yuyudhāna together rushed upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: vyāyacchamānāḥ subhṛśaṃ kurupāṇḍavasṛñjayāḥ priyān asūn raṇe tyaktvā yodhā jagmuḥ parasparam
english: Striving with all their might, the Kuru, Pāṇḍava, and Sṛñjaya warriors, casting away their dear lives in battle, closed with one another.

sanskrit: susaṃnaddhāḥ kavacinaḥ saśirastrāṇabhūṣaṇāḥ gadābhir musalaiś cānye parighaiś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Well-girt, mailed, adorned with helmets, the great car-warriors — some with maces, some with clubs, and others with iron bars —

sanskrit: samabhyadhāvanta bhṛśaṃ devā daṇḍair ivodyataiḥ nadantaś cāhvayantaś ca pravalgantaś ca māriṣa
english: rushed fiercely upon each other, like gods with raised rods, roaring, challenging, and bounding about, O honoured one.

sanskrit: tato nijaghnur anyonyaṃ petuś cāhavatāḍitāḥ vamanto rudhiraṃ gātrair vimastiṣkekṣaṇā yudhi
english: Then they slew one another and fell, smitten in the fray, vomiting blood from their limbs, their brains and eyes dashed out in battle.

sanskrit: dantapūrṇaiḥ sarudhirair vaktrair dāḍimasaṃnibhaiḥ jīvanta iva cāpy ete tasthuḥ śastropabṛṃhitāḥ
english: With faces full of teeth, blood-smeared and red as pomegranates, propped upright by the weapons within them, these slain men yet stood as though alive.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ cāpy apare paṭṭiśair asibhis tathā śaktibhir bhiṇḍipālaiś ca nakharaprāsatomaraiḥ
english: And still others fell upon one another with spears, swords, lances, slings, claw-weapons, darts, and javelins,

sanskrit: tatakṣuś cicchiduś cānye bibhiduś cikṣipus tathā saṃcakartuś ca jaghnuś ca kruddhā nirbibhiduś ca ha
english: and others, in their wrath, hacked, cut, pierced, hurled, mangled, slew, and tore one another asunder.

sanskrit: petur anyonyanihatā vyasavo rudhirokṣitāḥ kṣarantaḥ svarasaṃ raktaṃ prakṛtāś candanā iva
english: Slain by one another, lifeless and drenched in gore, they fell, oozing their own bright blood like sandal trees that bleed their sap.

sanskrit: rathai rathā vinihatā hastinaś cāpi hastibhiḥ narā naravaraiḥ petur aśvāś cāśvaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Chariots were destroyed by chariots, elephants by elephants, men by foremost of men, and horses by horses fell in their thousands.

sanskrit: dhvajāḥ śirāṃsi cchatrāṇi dvipahastā nṛṇāṃ bhujāḥ kṣurair bhallārdhacandraiś ca chinnāḥ śastrāṇi tatyajuḥ
english: Standards, heads, parasols, elephants' trunks, and the arms of men, severed by razor-shafts, broad-heads, and crescent-blades, let fall their weapons.

sanskrit: narāṃś ca nāgāṃś ca rathān hayān mamṛdur āhave aśvārohair hatāḥ śūrāś chinnahastāś ca dantinaḥ
english: Men, elephants, chariots, and horses were crushed in the battle; the brave were slain by horsemen, and the tuskers had their trunks cut off.

sanskrit: sapatākā dhvajāḥ petur viśīrṇā iva parvatāḥ pattibhiś ca samāplutya dviradāḥ syandanās tathā
english: Standards with their banners fell like crumbling mountains; and foot-soldiers, swarming up, brought down both elephants and chariots.

sanskrit: prahatā hanyamānāś ca patitāś caiva sarvaśaḥ aśvārohāḥ samāsādya tvaritāḥ pattibhir hatāḥ sādibhiḥ pattisaṃghāś ca nihatā yudhi śerate
english: Smitten, being struck down, and fallen on every side, horsemen swiftly closed and were slain by foot-soldiers, and bands of foot-soldiers, killed by horsemen, lay slain upon the field.

sanskrit: mṛditānīva padmāni pramlānā iva ca srajaḥ hatānāṃ vadanāny āsan gātrāṇi ca mahāmate
english: Like crushed lotuses and withered garlands, O most wise one, were the faces and the limbs of the slain.

sanskrit: rūpāṇy atyarthakāmyāni dviradāśvanṛṇāṃ nṛpa samunnānīva vastrāṇi prāpur durdarśatāṃ param
english: The once exceedingly beautiful forms of elephants, horses, and men, O king, like soaked garments, became most grievous to look upon.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hastibhis tu mahāmātrās tava putreṇa coditāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ jighāṃsantaḥ kruddhāḥ pārṣatam abhyayuḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the elephant-riders, urged on by your son, wrathful and seeking to slay Dhṛṣṭadyumna, rushed with their elephants upon the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: prācyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca pravīrā gajayodhinaḥ aṅgā vaṅgāś ca puṇḍrāś ca māgadhās tāmraliptakāḥ
english: The eastern and southern champions skilled in elephant-warfare — the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras, Māgadhas, and Tāmraliptakas,

sanskrit: mekalāḥ kośalā madrā daśārṇā niṣadhās tathā gajayuddheṣu kuśalāḥ kaliṅgaiḥ saha bhārata
english: the Mekalas, Kośalas, Madras, Daśārṇas, and Niṣadhas, skilled in elephant-battle, together with the Kaliṅgas, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: śaratomaranārācair vṛṣṭimanta ivāmbudāḥ siṣicus te tataḥ sarve pāñcālācalam āhave
english: all of these, like rain-laden clouds, drenched in the battle the mountain that was the Pāñcāla prince with arrows, lances, and iron shafts.

sanskrit: tān saṃmimardiṣur nāgān pārṣṇyaṅguṣṭhāṅkuśair bhṛśam pothitān pārṣato bāṇair nārācaiś cābhyavīvṛṣat
english: Eager to crush those elephants, sorely goaded by heels, toes, and hooks, the son of Pṛṣata drenched them with arrows and iron shafts.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ daśabhiḥ ṣaḍbhir aṣṭābhir api bhārata dviradān abhivivyādha kṣiptair girinibhāñ śaraiḥ pracchādyamāno dviradair meghair iva divākaraḥ
english: Each one of those mountain-like elephants he pierced with ten, with six, or with eight arrows hurled at them, O Bhārata, even as he was being veiled by the elephants like the sun by clouds.

sanskrit: paryāsuḥ pāṇḍupāñcālā nadanto niśitāyudhāḥ tān nāgān abhivarṣanto jyātantrīśaranāditaiḥ
english: The Pāṇḍus and Pāñcālas, roaring, their weapons whetted, surrounded those elephants, raining upon them with the twang of bowstrings and the cry of arrows.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca draupadeyāḥ prabhadrakāḥ sātyakiś ca śikhaṇḍī ca cekitānaś ca vīryavān
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, the sons of Draupadī, the Prabhadrakas, Sātyaki, Śikhaṇḍin, and the valiant Cekitāna —

sanskrit: te mlecchaiḥ preṣitā nāgā narān aśvān rathān api hastair ākṣipya mamṛduḥ padbhiś cāpy atimanyavaḥ
english: those elephants, sped on by the barbarians, seizing men, horses, and chariots with their trunks, in their great fury crushed them underfoot.

sanskrit: bibhiduś ca viṣāṇāgraiḥ samākṣipya ca cikṣipuḥ viṣāṇalagnaiś cāpy anye paripetur vibhīṣaṇāḥ
english: They gored with the points of their tusks, snatched up and flung men about, and others, terrible to behold, rushed on with bodies impaled upon their tusks.

sanskrit: pramukhe vartamānaṃ tu dvipaṃ vaṅgasya sātyakiḥ nārācenogravegena bhittvā marmaṇy apātayat
english: But the elephant of the Vaṅga that stood at the forefront, Sātyaki, piercing it in a vital spot with an iron shaft of terrible speed, brought down.

sanskrit: tasyāvarjitanāgasya dviradād utpatiṣyataḥ nārācenābhinad vakṣaḥ so 'patad bhuvi sātyakeḥ
english: As that warrior, his elephant felled, was springing down from it, Sātyaki pierced his breast with an iron shaft, and he fell to the earth.

sanskrit: puṇḍrasyāpatato nāgaṃ calantam iva parvatam sahadevaḥ prayatnāt tair nārācair vyahanat tribhiḥ
english: As the Puṇḍra's elephant, like a moving mountain, came rushing on, Sahadeva with effort struck it down with three iron shafts.
